limited_overlap.description: 893 of 12000 training applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their median prior earnings are 76,760 dollars. Their effects are extrapolated from the other applicants.
167 of 4000 new applicants have a fitted enrolment probability below 0.02; their predicted effects rest on extrapolation.

warnings: Follow-up survey response: 10119 of 12000 applicants answered (84.3%). Response depends on enrolment (logit coefficient 0.45 per enrolment). Results assume response is random given the covariates and enrolment; nothing in the data tests this, and response that depends on unobserved earnings would bias every estimate.
Final model: linear. RScorer (held-out responders): linear=-0.0013, causal_forest=-0.0015.

Instrument check: distance_km first-stage t statistic given covariates = -9.6; its direct t statistic in the follow-up earnings regression = -0.05. Distance-based IV estimate of the ATE = 5201 (90% -5478 to 15880).

Conditional-on-employment earnings effect = 4606 (90% 3737 to 5475); this compares employed applicants only, so it is not a causal effect on earnings of the employed unless employment is unaffected by enrolment.

Omitted-confounder benchmark: ATE when each strong confounder is dropped from the adjustment set: without prior_earnings = -4270, without months_unemployed = 4057, without education = 3794; full model = 4042.
Run time 10 seconds with seed 1; training rows 12000, responders 10119.
